actions.action: Move plant into a nursery pot with drainage holes set inside the galvanized container
Alternatively drill a drainage hole in the planter
Check top 2-3 inches of soil with finger before watering
Water thoroughly when dry and empty collected water
Slide plant out and inspect roots and stems
Trim black, mushy or smelly roots or stems
Cut off badly damaged mostly-brown leaves
Place in bright indirect light away from direct sun
Set up a pebble tray for humidity
Alternatively group plants together for humidity
Move pot away from heaters and cold drafts
If stems turn black and mushy, cut back to healthy tissue or propagate a healthy section in water
Report watering frequency, light and whether stems were cuttings

reason: The answer flags wet soil and no drainage but misses the dense soil mix and low light, and its advice to fix drainage omits switching to a chunky aroid mix and adding light, without being harmful.
